comments.note: APICacheManager.getCacheFolder() calls Application::getStorageSubfolderPath() which eagerly creates the cache folder on first access. This means getCacheSize() will return 0 (not an error), but it also creates an empty folder even when no cache has ever been written. This is consistent with the AICacheLocation pattern in the codebase, so it is acceptable.

The Application::getStorageSubfolderPath() method caches known subfolder paths in a static array. If clearAll() deletes the cache folder after the path has been cached, subsequent calls to getStorageSubfolderPath('api/cache') return the cached path without recreating the folder. Consumers must check folder existence themselves. getCacheManager already does this, but it should be noted for future maintainers.

comments.note: The WP requirement description specifies clearAll() should 'delete and recreate' the cache folder, but the implementation only deletes without recreating. The AC as written ('removes all cached data') is fully satisfied. Lazy recreation occurs through Application::getStorageSubfolderPath() on the next getCacheFolder() call, which is consistent with the AICacheLocation.clear() pattern. AC passes but the recreation note in the WP requirement is worth harmonising with the implementation.

getMethodCacheFolder(string $methodName) builds a path by appending $methodName directly without sanitisation. If an unsanitised external value ever reaches this (e.g. '../secret'), path traversal is possible. In current usage $methodName is an internal API method class name resolved at runtime, so risk is low. Recommend asserting the method name is non-empty and contains no directory separators before appending.

invalidateMethod('') with an empty string would produce the same path as the root cache folder, deleting ALL cached data. A guard (e.g. !empty($methodName)) in invalidateMethod() and getMethodCacheFolder() would make this more robust.

FileHelper::deleteTree(), FolderInfo::factory(), and folder->getSize() patterns are all confirmed correct by cross-reference with Application\AI\Cache\AICacheLocation (the established parallel implementation).

comments.note: APICacheManager is clean, fully static, well-documented with docblocks on every method. Follows established Application\AI\Cache patterns (AICacheLocation). No over-engineering. All 5 AC met.

SECURITY/DEFENSIVE: getMethodCacheFolder(string $methodName) appends $methodName directly to the storage path with no sanitisation. Current callers pass internal API method class names (e.g. 'MyAPIMethod') so no real-world path traversal risk exists today. However, a future caller passing an unsanitised external value could produce ../escape sequences. Recommend asserting strlen($methodName) > 0 && strpos($methodName, DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR) === false (or strpos($methodName, '..') === false) at the top of the method. This is a defensive coding improvement, not a current vulnerability.

DEFENSIVE: invalidateMethod('') would resolve to the same path as the base cache folder (since empty string concatenation produces '.../api/cache/'), resulting in clearAll()-equivalent behaviour. Adding a guard such as if(empty($methodName)) { return; } in invalidateMethod() and/or getMethodCacheFolder() would prevent this silent footgun for future callers.

SPEC DIVERGENCE (non-blocking): WP-002 requirement text says clearAll() should 'delete and recreate' the cache folder, but implementation only deletes. The accepted AC ('removes all cached data') is satisfied. Lazy recreation via getCacheFolder() on next access is consistent with the AICacheLocation.clear() pattern and is correct. However, the WP spec description should be updated to reflect the lazy-recreation design decision, to avoid confusing future maintainers who read the requirements.

getCacheSize() calls getCacheFolder() which eagerly creates the cache folder via Application::getStorageSubfolderPath(). This means calling getCacheSize() on a freshly cleared cache will recreate the folder as a side effect before checking existence. Behaviour is correct (returns 0 for empty folder) but the eager-creation side effect is invisible to callers. This matches the established AI cache pattern so no change required now.
